body: This usually happens when the mypy install is broken or site-packages is in the path. How did you install mypy? Can you look for `/usr/local/Cellar/python3/3.6.4/Frameworks/Python.framework/Versions/3.6/lib/mypy`? If it doesn't exist, your install is broken. Otherwise, you might try install mypy from git, I've added some better debugging about how site-packages got into the `PATH`.
Thanks — I installed through pip3, and no amount of uninstall/install would resolve the problem, but it installed fine through git as you suggested.

I'd like to reopen this, because we've seen this internally too -- a user has installed Python 3 via brew (/Cellar/ in the path is the giveaway here), installed mypy using pip3, and then somehow mypy can't find typeshed resulting in this crash. It doesn't happen to everyone who uses brew though, and IIRC there's a way to fix it that doesn't require installing from git master (something with `brew update` and/or upgrading Python 3 perhaps).
Sounds good. I’m happy to run anything if it would be helpful. I will note that after `pip3 install mypy` there was indeed no `mypy` file at the path noted by @ethanhs above.

If you could uninstall the git version and re-install normally, is there any folder named `typeshed` on your computer?

Also, I am going to up the priority of #5307, since we keep running into issues with data_files.

issue.title: Rethink how we package typeshed
issue.body:
Currently, we have a rather complicated method of finding data files. The current method we use to distribute typeshed is [ripe](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/5300) [for](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/5121) [issues](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/5022) [with](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/4852) [finding](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3988) [the](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3761) [files](https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/3211).

I think we should stop playing whack-a-mole with issues and ship typeshed differently. Here are two ideas:

1. Ship typeshed as a subpackage of mypy, while still keeping it a module. I originally proposed this in https://github.com/python/mypy/issues/4143 but was hung up on the symlinks in typeshed (which no longer exist). This would involve:
    - moving the submodule into the mypy package.
    - updating setup.py to use package_data
    - adding these files to MANIFEST.in to be picked up in sdists
2. Release typeshed as its own package and pin to a particular version. This was attempted in https://github.com/python/typeshed/pull/2025 but it was abandoned.

I have no particular preference for one over the other, but I think both are better than the current method.

body:
Sorry to ask, but how do I uninstall from the git repo? Googling didn't turn up much. Is
````
rm $(which mypy)
rm -rf /usr/local/lib/python3.6/site-packages/*mypy*
````
sufficient? If so, after doing that, reinstalling mypy (`pip3 install mypy`), mypy still fails, and there is no typeshed folder, at least not where I looked:

```
find /usr/local/lib/python3.6/site-packages -name typshed
# → returns nothing
```

You can uninstall via `pip uninstall mypy` for future reference (sorry I probably should have mentioned that). 

The typeshed folder is usually located outside of the site-packages, so it might be more useful to do `find /usr/local -name typeshed`. Hopefully this isn't horribly slow, if it is, you might try narrowing it to `/usr/local/Cellar`, which should help. Thank you for working with me on debugging this!

Ok, I didn't realize I could uninstall with pip after installing with git. Though it makes sense.

I ran the following:
```
pip3 uninstall mypy
find /usr/local -name typeshed # → nothing
pip3 install mypy
find /usr/local -name typeshed # → /usr/local/lib/mypy/typeshed
```
But now the original error is back.

Aha! That confirms my theory. It looks like data files are installed in a different root than the mypy package (`/usr/local/lib/` rather than `/usr/local/Cellar/`). Thanks so much for debugging this! 

For now, I'd suggest using mypy from git again if you can, but hopefully we can figure out a fix before the next release (which is soon).
Cool, glad I could help! I'm happy to use the workaround. Thanks for helping me out.

issue.title: added negative constraints

repository.name: sockeye
repository.description: Sequence-to-sequence framework with a focus on Neural Machine Translation based on PyTorch

issue.body:
This implements negative constraints in beam search, i.e., phrases that are not permitted to appear in the output. It works by tracking the progress of each negative constraint; if the last word is reached, the corresponding entry in the `scores` array is set to `np.inf` prior to the call to `topk()`.

issue.title: Use package_data to ship typeshed and xml files
issue.body:
Data files have caused many issues where mypy cannot find typeshed.
Using package_data allows us to find typeshed relative to the mypy
package itself, which avoids a lot of fragile path computation.

Fixes #5307 
Fixes #5319
